2027-03-15.title: Monday of the Fifth Week of Lent
readings: I am to die, though I have done none of the wicked things they charge against me
If I should walk in the valley of darkness, no evil would I fear, for you are there with me
Let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her
2027-03-15.alt: Lenten weekday of the fifth week. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. From the Fifth Sunday of Lent crosses and images may be veiled until the Passion is celebrated (where the bishops' conference allows). Liturgical colour: violet. The shorter form of the first reading begins at Daniel 13:41c.
2027-03-15.verse: Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.”
theo: The last fortnight of Lent opens with two women on trial. The first is Susanna, from the Greek chapters of Daniel. She is innocent. Two elders, judges of the people, lust after her and trap her alone in her husband's garden: give in, or we will swear we caught you with a young man. Her answer is one of the bravest sentences in the Bible: “I choose not to do it; I will fall into your hands, rather than sin in the sight of the Lord.” The elders keep their threat, the assembly believes them because they are elders, and she is condemned to death. Through her tears she looks up to heaven and prays: “O eternal God, you know what is secret and are aware of all things before they come to be.” The Lord hears her. He stirs up the spirit of a young lad named Daniel, who cries out, “I want no part in shedding this woman's blood!” He separates the two witnesses and asks each a simple question: under what tree? One says a mastic tree, the other an evergreen oak, and the lie collapses. The whole assembly blesses God, “who saves those who hope in him.” The Psalm is Susanna's prayer and ours: even in the darkest valley I fear no evil, for you are with me.

The second woman is guilty. Early in the morning, in the Temple, the scribes and Pharisees set before Jesus a woman caught in adultery: Moses commanded such women to be stoned; “Now what do you say?” It is a trap for him more than a trial for her. Jesus bends down and writes with his finger on the ground. When they press him, he stands and says: “Let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her.” Then he writes again. One by one they go away, “beginning with the elders.” St Augustine's famous phrase sums up the scene: two were left, misery and mercy. Jesus does not pretend that sin is nothing. He says both things: “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.” Put the two readings side by side and Lent becomes clear. God defends the innocent who trust him, and he lifts up the guilty who come before him. What he will not tolerate is the hard heart that stands ready with a stone. As the crosses are veiled and the Passion draws near, we are invited to drop our stones, to stop judging, and to let Jesus speak to us the word of pardon and of new life.
outline: Ask: have you ever been judged unfairly, or judged someone else too quickly?
Point 2 · The God who sees in secret
Daniel's wisdom and the collapse of the lie.
Jesus, the woman and the stones.
“Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.”
live: Name one person you have been judging harshly, and pray for them by name today.
Where you are being pressed to do wrong, decide today, with Susanna, to say no.
2027-03-15.prayer: O God, you defend the innocent who hope in you and you pardon the sinner who turns to you. Give us the courage of Susanna, who chose death rather than sin, and the humility to drop the stones we hold against others. Speak to us your word of mercy, Lord Jesus, and send us on our way to sin no more. Amen.
altar: At every Mass we say: Lord, I am not worthy. No one approaches the altar without sin; we come because the one who did not condemn the woman invites us to his table and makes us new.

quick: Susanna chose to fall into the hands of the wicked rather than sin before the Lord.
God heard her prayer and raised up Daniel to defend her.
Jesus refused to condemn the sinful woman and told her to sin no more.
2027-03-15.action: Put down one judgment today: say nothing critical about anyone until bedtime.
2027-03-15.question: Am I standing in the crowd with a stone, or kneeling before Jesus asking for mercy?

family.explain: Some men brought a woman who had done wrong and wanted to throw stones at her. Jesus said: whoever has never sinned can throw the first stone. Nobody could! They all went away. Jesus forgave her and said: go, and do not sin again.
family.intention: We pray for people who are judged unfairly, and for all who need forgiveness.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family or class we have been unkind to or have judged? How can we make it right?”

illus: A story told in a Thrissur parish: a woman was accused in the neighbourhood of stealing from the house where she worked. The gossip spread quickly. Only one old neighbour refused to repeat it, saying: I was not there, and neither were you. A week later the missing money was found where the owner himself had put it away. The women who had talked went to her one by one to say sorry. She told the parish priest later that the old neighbour's silence had been her Daniel.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you did not condemn the sinner, and you defended the innocent. Teach us mercy and give us courage. Amen.
share: I choose not to do it… rather than sin in the sight of the Lord (Daniel 13:23). Where do I need Susanna's courage?
Let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone (John 8:7). Whom am I quick to judge?
Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again (John 8:11). Which sin do I need to leave behind this Lent?
pm.resp: Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I fear no evil; for you are with me.
interc: For those falsely accused, in courts, workplaces and families, that the truth may come to light.
For judges, police and lawyers, that they may be honest and fair.
For women and girls who suffer abuse and threats, that they may be protected and believed.
For all who are ashamed of their sins, that they may meet the mercy of Jesus in confession.
For our group, that we may never use our tongues as stones.
pm.close: Father, you see what is secret and you save those who hope in you. Make us merciful as your Son is merciful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we meet two women on trial. Susanna is innocent. Two elders, judges of the people, try to force her into sin and threaten to accuse her falsely if she refuses. She answers: I choose not to do it; I will fall into your hands, rather than sin in the sight of the Lord (Daniel 13:23). She would rather lose her life than lose God.

Condemned by a court that believed the elders, she prays: O eternal God, you know what is secret (Daniel 13:42). And God raises up young Daniel, who exposes the lie with one question: under what tree? The assembly blesses God, who saves those who hope in him. God sees, and God defends.

The second woman is guilty. Her accusers want to use her to trap Jesus. He writes on the ground and says: let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her (John 8:7). They go away, one by one, beginning with the eldest. Only Jesus and the woman remain: misery and mercy, as St Augustine says.

Jesus says: neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again (John 8:11). He does not call sin nothing; he gives her a new beginning. This week, as we draw close to the cross, let us drop our stones, go to confession, and hear those same words spoken to us. Amen.
kids: Children, some people wanted to throw stones at a woman who had done wrong. Jesus said: only someone who has never sinned can throw the first stone. Nobody could! Jesus forgave her. Today, instead of saying unkind words about someone, let us say a kind word or a prayer for them.

intro: Theme: “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.”
The innocent defended, the guilty forgiven, the stones dropped.

sub: Fear God, not those who kill the body.
q: I choose not to do it; I will fall into your hands, rather than sin in the sight of the Lord.
Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
points.apply: Where you are under pressure to do wrong, say no today and tell God you trust him with the cost.

points.h: The God who sees in secret
q: O eternal God, you know what is secret and are aware of all things before they come to be;
And before him no creature is hidden, but all are naked and laid bare to the eyes of the one to whom we must render an account.
points.apply: Refuse to pass on any story about another person that you have not seen for yourself.

sub: Not condemned, but sent to sin no more.
q: As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live;

Jesus straightened up and said to her, “Woman, where are they? Has no one condemned you?” She said, “No one, sir.” And Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.”
points.apply: Go to confession before Holy Week, and leave behind the sin Jesus names in your heart.

concl: God defends those who hope in him and forgives those who come to him.
Only the hard heart with a stone in its hand keeps itself away from mercy.
2027-03-15.resolve: Say no unkind word about anyone this week, and make your Easter confession.
